quotes.text: Learn about Cartes Bancaires, a common payment method in France.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: If a charge is declined on the Cartes Bancaires network for a technical reason, Stripe
More than 95% of these cards are co-badged with either Visa or Mastercard
If your business isn’t based in France, you must first process one payment from a Cartes Bancaires eligible card to fully enable this payment method.
Businesses can’t contest Cartes Bancaires disputes. The dispute fee is 0 EUR on Cartes Bancaires.
Express Checkout Element doesn’t support Cartes Bancaires.

findings: The November 7 capture is a 14-line Cartes Bancaires overview/index with iOS and Web variant links; neither variant body is captured (new raw lines 5-14). It establishes the page topic and navigation only, not current eligibility, integration steps, pricing, routing, dispute rules, or platform support.

The May 1 full capture describes France's CB card network, >95% co-badged Visa/Mastercard share, EEA customer network-choice statement, and fallback to Visa/Mastercard only after a technical-reason CB network decline (old raw lines 8-10). The source line 17 says Stripe auto-retries if CB declines without the technical-reason condition; correct that materially broader claim.

May guide property table gives Europe customer locations, EUR presentment, customer-initiated confirmation, card family, recurring payments, standard payout timing, Connect, disputes, manual/multicapture and full/partial refunds (old raw lines 12-56). Its 41 listed Stripe-account business countries (old raw lines 58-102) and product routes with Express Checkout Element and Terminal caveats (old raw lines 104-114) are dated, not renewed by November links. Source lines 13 and 23 retain important subset but should not imply current universal availability.

The May availability prerequisite applies only to a business outside France and requires one payment from a CB-eligible card to fully enable the method (old raw lines 116-118). Source line 19 and linked Cartes Bancaires concept line 22 omit the eligible-card qualifier, risking an incorrect enablement conclusion; add reciprocal correction with May provenance.

The May dispute section says lower dispute rate on average because fewer dispute reasons, no Stripe contest route, 0 EUR fee and possible withdrawn dispute marked won (old raw lines 120-126). Source lines 13 and 21 correctly mention these but should remain May snapshot claims. The Cartes Bancaires concept already distinguishes Adyen's separate automatic-defense route (concept line 34); do not generalize Stripe's no-contest statement to all providers.

The May integration note says already accepting card payments is a route to CB acceptance, directs readers to separate co-badged choice/test-card guidance, and says to contact Stripe Support if CB must never default (old raw lines 128-130). This is historical documentation, not evidence of account eligibility or a successful charge.
substantive_changes: No CB processing, dispute or availability change can be concluded from the new root capture; the diff replaces May detailed text with iOS/Web navigation (diff lines 3-14, 129-132; new raw lines 9-14).

Source correction is still required independently of the navigation-only raw delta: source line 17 omits the technical-decline trigger, and line 19 omits the CB-eligible-card condition (old raw lines 10, 118).
historical_claims_to_preserve: As of May 1, 2026, >95% co-badged Visa/Mastercard statement and EEA customer-choice guidance, with the linked separate compliance guide; treat legal scope as Stripe's dated statement (old raw line 8).
As of May 1, 2026, technical-decline-only Visa/Mastercard retry claim, not a promise of automatic retry after any decline or ultimate authorization (old raw line 10).
As of May 1, 2026, EUR presentment, 41 listed account countries, product routes and Express Checkout Element/Terminal qualifications (old raw lines 12-114).
As of May 1, 2026, non-France prerequisite of one CB-eligible-card payment for full enablement; Stripe-specific dispute rules and 0 EUR fee (old raw lines 116-126).
conflicts: Source-stripe-cartes-bancaires.md:17 says Stripe retries on Visa/Mastercard if CB declines; old raw line 10 limits that automatic retry to technical-reason network declines. Correct source and avoid treating retry as success.

Source-stripe-cartes-bancaires.md:19 and wiki/concepts/cartes-bancaires.md:22 omit that the initial payment outside France must be from a CB-eligible card for full enablement (old raw line 118); apply a reciprocal dated correction.

The November root's iOS/Web links (new raw lines 13-14) do not revalidate May country, dispute, fee, regulatory or feature claims; neither linked variant was read. Existing co-badged-cards concept lines 10-18 already carries an Adyen-versus-Stripe scope warning that should not be collapsed.
unresolved_questions: The November iOS and Web variant bodies were not captured; any current platform-specific acceptance, configuration, regional rules, eligibility or disputes remain unverified by this unit.

findings: Add separately dated November iOS/Web index provenance, retaining May 1 claims under May raw only (source lines 4-13, 25-27; new raw lines 9-14).
Restrict Visa/Mastercard automatic retry claim to CB technical-reason declines and avoid implying successful fallback (source line 17; old raw line 10).
Specify CB-eligible-card first payment for non-France full enablement and note reciprocal omission at wiki/concepts/cartes-bancaires.md:22 (source line 19; old raw line 118).
Keep May business-country, EUR, dispute fee/no-contest, product support and legal guidance dated and provider-specific (source lines 13-23; old raw lines 8, 18-114, 120-130).
conflicts: Source line 17 broadens technical-decline-only fallback to any CB decline.
Source line 19 and linked concept line 22 omit the eligible-card prerequisite.
source_assessments.reason: November adds only platform navigation, but the existing source overstates retry and omits a material non-France enablement condition; both axes require a source update.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/cartes-bancaires, new raw lines 5-14 establish only a CB overview and links to iOS and Web variants; no current platform procedure or lifecycle rule appears in the pinned root. The May guide, old raw lines 8-10, 12-118 and 120-130, historically describes co-badged cards, EUR presentment, listed account countries, product support, technical-decline-only network fallback, non-France full enablement after one CB-eligible-card payment, and Stripe-specific dispute conditions. The mapped source-stripe-cartes-bancaires.md summarizes these May facts but source line 17 overgeneralizes retries to any decline and line 19 omits card eligibility. The linked Cartes Bancaires concept repeats the latter omission.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/cartes-bancaires, new raw lines 9-14 are iOS/Web navigation, not evidence of changed processing, availability, fees, disputes or legal obligations. Preserve the May 1, 2026 claims from old raw lines 8-10, 12-118 and 120-130 as dated and provider-specific. In source-stripe-cartes-bancaires.md, source lines 17-19 need reciprocal warnings: fallback was documented only for technical CB declines, and non-France full enablement requires a CB-eligible-card payment; wiki/concepts/cartes-bancaires.md:22 repeats the latter omission. The old Express Checkout Element and Terminal caveats are platform-specific, and the unread November variant bodies cannot update them. A retry is not proof of authorization, a first payment statement is not account access evidence, and Stripe dispute limits do not govern Adyen.
